name: external-agents
description: Launch supported coding-agent CLIs, inspect their local session history, and attach bounded session context through a read-only workspace.
author: Localix

commands.name: claude
commands.description: Delegate a task to the Claude Code CLI, driving it interactively.

args.name: task
args.description: The work to hand off to Claude Code.
args.placeholder: implement the CSV parser and add tests

commands.prompt:
Delegate this task to the Claude Code CLI by DRIVING IT INTERACTIVELY in a terminal (bash actions: `open` / `screen` / `keys` / `type`). Read the screen at each step — never assume what is on it.

USER REQUEST (a terse note to YOU, not the literal prompt to send):

${task}

## 1. Refine the task
Turn the note above into ONE clear, self-contained instruction for Claude. Fix typos and vague phrasing; add the obvious expectation the user implied. Send the REFINED instruction — never the raw text.
- "just say hello" -> "Say hello."
- "fix login" -> "Investigate and fix the login bug, then run the tests."

CLI check: !`command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "claude: available" || echo "claude: MISSING - tell the user to install Claude Code, then stop"`

## 2. Launch
Open a pane with a command in EXACTLY this shape — the leading declarations are how the workspace
recognizes the pane as a delegation and finds its transcript, so never strip them, reorder them, or
prepend a `cd`:

```
LOCALIX_AGENT=claude-code LOCALIX_AGENT_CWD='<absolute project dir>' claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
```

Add flags at the END only (` --model <alias>` if a specific tier is wanted: `opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku`/`fable`, which always resolve to the CURRENT latest of that tier; never a hardcoded model id).

## 3. Drive it
1. bash `action: open` with that command. `open` returns the initial screen (no separate `screen` needed unless it came back blank). The delegation now appears in the External Agents Workspace roster with live state; `external_agent_sessions { action: "roster" }` is where you read its key (`claude-code:<id>`).
2. ONLY if that screen was blank/cold-starting: bash `action: screen` once. On first-ever use it may show a one-time bypass-permissions warning — read it and confirm.
3. Send the REFINED task in ONE call: bash `action: type` with the task text AND `keys: ["Enter"]` together.

## 4. Knowing when it is done — OBSERVATION, not a report
Nothing is injected into Claude's prompt and it is NOT asked to report back: this plugin reads the
delegation's state from what can be observed — the rendered screen classified against a detection
manifest, and Claude's own transcript on disk. So do not ask it to message you, and do not invent a
protocol for it.

To learn when it settles, use ONE of these — never a screen-polling loop, and never `bash action:"wait"`
(that holds THIS turn open, which is strictly worse than ending it):
- `external_agent_sessions { action: "wait", keys: ["claude-code:<id>"], until: ["done", "blocked"], timeoutMs: 1800000 }`
  — bounded at 30 min, resolves immediately if the state already holds, and a timeout is a normal
  reported outcome. Keys come from `{ action: "roster" }`. With SEVERAL delegations add `mode: "any"`
  ("wake me when the first one needs a decision") or `mode: "all"` ("when all of them have finished").
- Or END YOUR TURN and pick the work up on your next turn with `{ action: "roster" }`.

## 5. On resume
bash `action: screen` once. If a menu is up, answer with the matching number / arrow keys + Enter,
then settle again. Never guess — the screen shows the current choices.

## 6. Finish
When the state is `done`/`idle`, read the result with `action: screen`. Exit with `keys: ["Ctrl+C","Ctrl+C"]` (twice — the reliable exit), then bash
`action: close`. Then report to the USER what Claude changed and its result — you write that summary
from what you read, because nothing else will.

## Reference
For the full reference (every flag, headless `-p` mode, in-session slash commands, approval menus, models, gotchas) read the `driving-claude-code` skill with the skill tool.


delegation's state from what can be observed — the rendered screen classified against a detection

- `external_agent_sessions { action: "wait", keys: ["codex:<id>"], until: ["done", "blocked"], timeoutMs: 1800000 }`
  — bounded at 30 min, resolves immediately if the state already holds, and a timeout is a normal

  ("wake me when the first one needs a decision") or `mode: "all"` ("when all of them have finished").

then settle again. Never guess — the screen shows the current choices.

## 6. Finish
When the state is `done`/`idle`, read the result with `action: screen`. Exit with `keys: ["Ctrl+C"]` (press twice if it shows a press-again-to-quit prompt), or a quit slash-command shown on screen, then bash
`action: close`. Then report to the USER what Codex changed and its result — you write that summary
from what you read, because nothing else will.
